```cs
    public ValueTask<string> GetGenerationAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        => ValueTask.FromResult(_generations.GetOrAdd(key, _ => Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")));

    // Called after a successful POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE: a fresh generation hides every older response.
    public ValueTask InvalidateAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        _generations[key] = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }

    public ValueTask<HttpCacheEntry?> GetAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        => ValueTask.FromResult(_entries.TryGetValue(key, out var stored) && stored.Expires > time.GetUtcNow() ? stored.Entry : null);

    public ValueTask SetAsync(string key, HttpCacheEntry entry, TimeSpan timeToLive, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        _entries[key] = (entry, time.GetUtcNow() + timeToLive);
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }

    public ValueTask RemoveAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        _entries.TryRemove(key, out _);
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }

    public ValueTask ClearAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        _generations.Clear(); // in-flight requests can then only publish into orphaned generations
        _entries.Clear();
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }
}
```

A production storage also bounds its generation records (the built-in one groups URLs into 4096 slots). Register it
before `AddHttpCaching()`:

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IHttpCacheStorage>(new DictionaryHttpCacheStorage(TimeProvider.System));
builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IGitHubClient, GitHubClient>()
    .AddHttpCaching();
```

## Transport and cookies

`AddHttpCaching()` turns off automatic cookies on the client's `SocketsHttpHandler` or `HttpClientHandler`, after all
other configuration of that handler, so the default registration caches at once. Other named clients are unaffected.
A handler that already has cookies off is left alone, so a cookie-free handler shared between clients keeps working.
`ConfigureHttpClientDefaults(b => b.AddHttpCaching())` caches every client, each under its own name: two clients
never share entries, and they all use the settings given there.
Send caller cookies as request headers; a handler that keeps a hidden cookie jar belongs on a client without HTTP
caching.

The cache runs after every other handler you add, so caller identity and rewritten requests are visible before
lookup.

Other transports (wrappers the cache can't see into, native platform handlers), and handlers inside the primary
transport or below a cache handler you construct yourself, can't be checked. They bypass caching and log one warning
per named client, unless you set `AllowUnverifiedTransport`. Set it only when you have checked that the whole
transport sends no automatic cookies or hidden caller identity. A known transport with automatic cookies turned on
always bypasses.

HTTP cache freshness includes request/response delay when correcting the upstream Age header, for both initial responses and 304 validation. Age arithmetic saturates instead of overflowing on extreme headers.

Background HTTP revalidation preserves the request HTTP version, version policy and a shallow copy of its request options. Option values keep their original ownership; use values that remain valid for background work.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/distributed-cache.md -->

# Distributed cache

By default each application instance has its own in-memory cache. Add a distributed cache to share results between
instances and keep them across restarts:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");   // MethodCache.Redis
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheSqlServer(connectionString);   // MethodCache.SqlServer
```

Redis backplane publication stops waiting when its token is cancelled. A cancelled unsubscribe acknowledgement does not fail application shutdown. SQL backplane identity gaps are not forgotten just because a transaction took longer than five seconds: committed gap rows are read without waiting, and a separate `NOWAIT` locking probe confirms an older identity is absent before it is forgotten. A locked or timed-out probe leaves gaps available for retry while newer invalidations and other committed gap messages are delivered.

## How it works

- Results live in memory (L1) and in the distributed cache (L2). An in-memory miss reads the distributed cache before
  running your method, and a new result is written to both.
- Invalidating a key removes it from the distributed cache. Invalidating a tag records when it happened, so older
  entries with that tag read as misses. A backplane tells every other instance to drop its in-memory copy: at once
  with Redis pub/sub, or on their next poll (every second by default) with SQL Server.
- Only Redis and Microsoft SQL Server have packages. Another store, such as PostgreSQL, needs a
  [custom provider](#custom-distributed-caches).
- `[Cache]` methods and `GetOrCreateAsync` need no changes.
- MethodCache keeps its own distributed cache and connection, so your application's `IDistributedCache` is left alone.

Run the same MethodCache version on every instance that shares a cache and backplane; messages from another version
are ignored with one warning.

## When the distributed cache is down

Calls keep working from memory and your methods; the distributed cache never fails or stalls a call. Each call to it
is capped at `OperationTimeout` (one second), a circuit breaker skips it until it is back, and invalidations are queued and retried
instead of throwing. Until they are stored, the instance doesn't read entries from it, so an invalidated value can't
come back. The [health check](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md#health-check) reports Degraded while this lasts.

Queued invalidations are stored a batch at a time once the cache answers, so a long outage's backlog drains at the
pace the cache can take. More than 10,000 are replaced by one clear of the distributed cache (logged as a warning),
and so is an invalidation the cache keeps refusing while it answers everything else, so neither holds up the rest.
The queue lives in memory: when the instance shuts down, it waits for writes still running, then tries once more to store
what is queued, each step (stamp, removal, publish) capped by `OperationTimeout`, and logs a warning with the number it had to drop. Other instances can read those invalidated
values from the distributed cache until they expire.

A value set directly while the distributed cache is down stays in that instance's memory, and the value it replaced is
removed from the distributed cache and the other instances once it is back. An entry that comes back damaged (cut
short, or unreadable by the serializer) is a miss: your method runs and its result replaces the entry.

The timeout caps each call to the distributed cache, not a whole cache miss. A cache that stops answering costs a miss
one timeout, after which the circuit breaker skips it. One that answers just within the timeout costs a miss up to
three: reading the entry, writing your method's result and checking that no removal raced the write (and a fourth for
the backplane message).

## Options

`DistributedCacheOptions` apply to Redis, SQL Server and custom distributed caches alike:

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<DistributedCacheOptions>(options =>
{
    options.OperationTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
    options.CircuitBreakerDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
});
```

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `OperationTimeout` | 1 second | The longest one call to the distributed cache may take. A slower call is abandoned and counts as a failure, except a write (see [What other instances see](#what-other-instances-see)) |
| `CircuitBreakerDuration` | 10 seconds | How long the distributed cache is skipped after a failure or timeout. Invalidations it didn't accept are retried at this interval |
| `ClockSkewTolerance` | 2 seconds | How far apart your servers' clocks may be. A tag invalidation also applies to entries created up to this long after it. One stamped further ahead of an instance's clock (by a server whose clock runs fast) counts from when that instance first read it, until its clock reaches the stamp |
| `TagCheckInterval` | 1 second | How long an instance trusts the invalidation time it last read for a tag. Without a backplane, an entry read from the distributed cache can outlive a tag invalidation made on another instance by up to this long |
| `TagRetention` | 1 day | How long tag invalidations are kept. An entry stays in the distributed cache at most `TagRetention - ClockSkewTolerance` from when your method started loading it (less if its own duration is shorter); a load that takes longer is kept only in that instance's memory. Both values are truncated to whole milliseconds, and `TagRetention` must exceed `ClockSkewTolerance` by at least one millisecond, or startup fails; with SQL Server it must also end before 9999-12-31 |
| `KeyPrefix` | `methodcache:` | Prefix of every key MethodCache writes. `AddMethodCacheRedis` and `AddMethodCacheSqlServer` set it from their own `KeyPrefix`; give each application its own |

## What other instances see

- An invalidation reaches another instance when the backplane delivers it. Until then, and for good if the message is
  lost or the instance is disconnected from the backplane, that instance serves its in-memory copy until it expires,
  as without a backplane. Instances without a copy read the distributed cache, which is already right.
- Messages carry no values, so a late, repeated or reordered message only makes an instance read the distributed cache
  again.
- An invalidation the distributed cache didn't accept is retried every `CircuitBreakerDuration`. Until the retry
  succeeds, other instances can serve the old value; the instance that invalidated never does.
- A write that timed out (a large value, say) doesn't open the circuit breaker, since the cache may answer everything
  else: the instance logs a warning and keeps using it. Such a write may still land later, because a distributed cache
  has no compare-and-set, so its key is removed again after `CircuitBreakerDuration` (as after a write that failed,
  once the cache answers). Further timed-out writes of the key push that one removal back, and an instance that shuts
  down first removes the key while it shuts down. Until then the late value can replace a newer one, and a write that
  lands after that removal stays until it expires.
- Entries carry no checksum: damage that still reads as a valid value is served.

## Serialization

Values are written as JSON with System.Text.Json, public fields included, so value tuples and structs with fields
are shared as they are. Every value an instance writes is read back and written again first; when that doesn't give
the same bytes and type, that value and every later value of the method with that type stay in the instance's memory
only, and one warning names the method and the type. Each value is checked, since one with default data (an `Id` of
0 behind a private setter) can come back unchanged where the next one doesn't. A serializer that never writes the same
bytes twice (encryption with a fresh nonce) can't be compared that way, so for it only the type is checked. State
the serializer never writes at all (a class that keeps its data only in private fields, which JSON writes as `{}`)
reads back as the same bytes, so the check can't see that it is lost: make such state serializable, or register a
serializer that writes it. That happens with properties that have a
private or protected setter, public readonly fields of a type that also has a parameterless constructor, a derived
type returned as its declared base type (an `Animal` method returning a `Dog`, even after it returned plain
`Animal`s), and `object`, with JSON and MessagePack alike. A value the serializer throws on (a cycle, a delegate
field) stays in memory the same way. A collection declared as an interface (`IReadOnlyList<int>`,
`IEnumerable<int>`) may come back as another implementation, a `List<int>` for an array, and is still shared. The
check looks at the type of the value itself, not of what it holds: a `Dog` inside a `List<Animal>` or in a property
declared `Animal` is shared without its `Dog` data. To share such values, register a serializer that reads them back,
such as `JsonCacheSerializer` with your own `JsonSerializerOptions` or `JsonSerializerContext` (`[JsonInclude]` on the
setter, `[JsonDerivedType]` on the base type), or your own `ISerializer`. The `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack` package makes values
smaller and faster to read:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheMessagePack();   // MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack
```

Entries written in the other format read as misses and are replaced, so switching needs no flush. See the
[MessagePack package guide](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack/README.md). Under Native AOT, register your
`JsonSerializerContext` ([Native AOT](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/native-aot.md)).

## Custom distributed caches

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheDistributedCache(
    _ => customCache);   // IDistributedCache with backend-atomic invalidation stamps
```

`customCache` implements `IAtomicInvalidationStore` (in `MethodCache.Extensibility`), which extends
`IDistributedCache`. MethodCache rejects a provider without this capability, such as Microsoft's
`MemoryDistributedCache` (`AddDistributedMemoryCache()`), `RedisCache` or `SqlServerCache`: with a generic host,
`host.StartAsync()` throws an `OptionsValidationException` naming `IAtomicInvalidationStore`, so the app fails at
startup rather than on its first request; without a host, resolving the cache manager throws an `ArgumentException`.
Implement `WriteInvalidationStampAsync` with a backend atomic maximum: keep the highest unexpired
signed timestamp, expose it as eight little-endian bytes through `GetAsync`, and never shorten an unexpired
stamp’s retention. Expired stamps can be replaced. A process-local lock or a read followed by `SetAsync` is
insufficient for a backend shared by different processes. Redis uses one Lua operation; SQL Server uses a
transaction with a key/range update lock. This applies to tag, clear and key-removal stamps.

The [HTTP response cache](http-caching.md) has its own contract and works with a plain `IDistributedCache`.

Without a backplane, other instances keep their in-memory copy of an invalidated entry until it expires. Register an
`IBackplane` (in `MethodCache.Extensibility`) to send invalidations to them. Disposing the service provider
unsubscribes from the backplane; a backplane that stalls delays disposal by at most twice `OperationTimeout`.

## Keep invalidations from being evicted

Tag, clear and key-removal stamps are ordinary expiring keys next to the entries they invalidate. A store that evicts a
stamp under memory pressure while an entry it invalidated stays makes that entry valid again, on every instance, until
it expires. Give the store room, and don't let it evict MethodCache's keys: for Redis, use `maxmemory-policy
noeviction` (or a Redis of its own). Every MethodCache key has a time to live, so the `volatile-*` policies can evict
them as well as the `allkeys-*` ones. With `noeviction`, a full Redis refuses writes instead: MethodCache then treats it
as down and answers from memory. SQL Server removes rows only once they expired.

## Limits

- Pattern invalidation (`InvalidateByTagPatternAsync`) throws `NotSupportedException` with a distributed cache.
- [Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md) values and [runtime overrides](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#runtime-overrides) live in each instance's
  memory.

## Package guides

The [Redis](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.Redis/README.md) and [SQL Server](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.SqlServer/README.md) READMEs
cover their options, shared connections, table creation, outage settings and how each stores keys and invalidations.
The SQL Server guide also compares the two and has the schema migration for an existing invalidations table.

An explicit `SetAsync` with a lifetime shorter than L2 millisecond precision removes the previous distributed value instead of leaving it readable. If the backend is unavailable, the removal follows the normal invalidation retry path.

Caller cancellation stops the wait during an L2 read or a slow factory, including bulk reads and fail-safe waits. Shared work may finish for other callers; cancellation is not reported as a dependency failure.

SQL Server backplane initialization requires a non-nullable `binary(32)` `Scope` column. Incompatible scope columns
are reported without automatic schema upgrades; see the [SQL Server guide](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.SqlServer/README.md#required-backplane-schema).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/monitoring.md -->

# Monitoring

MethodCache shows what it is doing in code, over HTTP, in health checks and through OpenTelemetry.

## In code

`ICacheAdministrator`, registered by `AddMethodCache()`, reads statistics, lists methods and entries, and invalidates:

```cs
var stats = await admin.GetStatsAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Hit ratio {stats.HitRatio:P0}, {stats.Entries} entries");

foreach (var method in admin.GetMethods())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{method.MethodId}: {method.Duration}");
}

var entries = admin.ListEntries(tag: "user:42");
await admin.InvalidateTagsAsync(["user:42"]);
```

- `GetStatsAsync()`: hits, misses, hit ratio, evictions, entries and estimated memory.
- `GetMethods()`: every cached method with its method id and effective policy.
- `ListEntries(keyPrefix, tag, limit)` and `GetEntry(key)`: live entries, without their values.
- `InvalidateTagsAsync(tags)`, `RemoveEntryAsync(key)` and `ClearAsync()`.

`ListEntries` returns entries in key order. It is a diagnostic scan, not a transaction: entries can change while it
runs.

It works with the default in-memory cache manager; a custom `ICacheManager` has no administrator.

## Admin endpoints

The `MethodCache.AspNetCore` package exposes the same operations over HTTP, behind an authorization policy you choose:

```cs
builder.Services.AddScoped<IUserService, UserService>();
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddAuthorization(o => o.AddPolicy("CacheAdmins", p => p.RequireRole("Admin")));

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapMethodCacheAdmin("CacheAdmins");
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
```

The [package README](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.AspNetCore/README.md#endpoints) lists every endpoint. They don't change
policies; use [runtime overrides](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#runtime-overrides) for that.

## Health check

`AddHealthChecks().AddMethodCache()`, from the same package, reports Degraded while Redis or SQL Server is unreachable
and MethodCache serves from memory only. The [package README](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.AspNetCore/README.md#health-check)
lists the data it reports.

## OpenTelemetry

The `MethodCache.OpenTelemetry` package records metrics for every call (hits, misses, errors and load time per
method, and the size of the in-memory cache) and spans for misses and invalidations:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheOpenTelemetry(); // after AddMethodCache, which registers the cache it instruments

builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
    .WithTracing(tracing => tracing
        .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
        .AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter())
    .WithMetrics(metrics => metrics
        .AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter());
```

Hits have no span and add no allocations. Cache keys and tags are left off spans unless you turn on `RecordCacheKeys`
or `RecordCacheTags`, because they can contain argument values. The
[package README](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/src/MethodCache.OpenTelemetry/README.md) lists the options, span attributes and metrics; see
also [Security](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/security.md#methodcacheopentelemetry).

## Your own metrics

Without OpenTelemetry, cache events go to an `ICacheMetricsProvider` (in `MethodCache.Extensibility`). The default
one discards them. To see them on the console while you develop:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddConsoleCacheMetrics();   // "Cache Hit: ...", "Cache Miss: ..." on standard output
```

Or implement the interface. Each cached call is reported once, as a hit or a miss; errors and load times are reported
when your method runs. `methodName` is the method id, such as `MyApp.IUserService.GetUserAsync`, the same id the admin
endpoints list (a generic interface reports its closed type, such as `IRepository<User>.Get`):

```cs
public sealed class CountingMetrics : ICacheMetricsProvider
{
    private long _hits, _misses, _errors;

    public long Hits => Interlocked.Read(ref _hits);
    public long Misses => Interlocked.Read(ref _misses);
    public long Errors => Interlocked.Read(ref _errors);

    public void CacheHit(string methodName) => Interlocked.Increment(ref _hits);
    public void CacheMiss(string methodName) => Interlocked.Increment(ref _misses);
    public void CacheError(string methodName, string errorMessage) => Interlocked.Increment(ref _errors);
    public void CacheLatency(string methodName, TimeSpan elapsed) { }   // load time after a miss
}
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddSingleton<ICacheMetricsProvider, CountingMetrics>();
```

One provider receives the events: the last one registered. `AddMethodCacheOpenTelemetry()` registers its own, so use
it or a provider of your own, not both; with `EnableMetrics = false` it leaves yours in place and adds only spans. A custom `ICacheManager` reports its own hits and misses. If you wrap
`ICacheManager` in a decorator of your own, implement `ICacheManagerDecorator` so `GetOrCreateManyAsync` still reads
the distributed cache through it.

OpenTelemetry instruments the unkeyed `ICacheManager` registration and leaves unrelated keyed managers untouched. A keyed-only registration does not satisfy its requirement for a default manager.

OpenTelemetry preserves the original cache manager registration lifetime and DI disposal ownership. Type/factory-created managers remain container-owned; supplied instances remain caller-owned, including asynchronous disposal.

An instrumented cache lookup generates the application cache key once and reuses it for tracing and the presence-aware inner lookup, preserving the original method and arguments without a second serialization/hash pass.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/memory-cache.md -->

# Memory cache

The in-memory cache uses W-TinyLFU eviction by default: when it is full, it keeps the entries that are read often and
evicts the rest, so a burst of one-off reads doesn't push out your hot data. Configure it with
`MethodCacheMemoryOptions`:

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<MethodCacheMemoryOptions>(o =>
{
    o.MaxItems = 50_000;                              // default 10,000
    o.DefaultExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10);   // for methods without a Duration; default 5 minutes
    o.JitterMaxDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);   // spread out entries created together
    o.CacheNullValues = false;                        // a null result means "try again next time"
});
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| `MaxItems` | 10,000 | The most entries kept |
| `MaxMemoryBytes` | 1000 MB | The most total weight kept; used only with a `Weigher` |
| `Weigher` | none | Returns an entry's cost, for example its size in bytes |
| `EvictionPolicy` | `TinyLfu` | What to evict when full: `TinyLfu`, `Lru` (least recently read) or `Fifo` (oldest stored) |
| `DefaultExpiration` | 5 minutes | The duration of methods with none of their own and no `DefaultPolicy` |
| `MaxExpiration` | 7 days | No entry lives longer, whatever its duration |
| `JitterMaxDuration` | zero | Adds a random extra lifetime up to this value, so entries created together don't expire together |
| `CacheNullValues` | `true` | Caches `null` results like any other value |
| `EnableStatistics` | `true` | Counts hits, misses and evictions for the [statistics](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md) |
| `EnableFastPath` | `true` | Generated decorators answer hits from a lookup that allocates nothing; turning it off only makes hits slower |
| `EnableBackgroundCleanup` | `true` | Removes expired entries on a timer, not only when they are read |
| `CleanupInterval` | 1 minute | How often the background cleanup runs; 10 seconds to 24 hours |
| `MemoryCalculationMode` | `Fast` | How `MemoryUsage` in the statistics is estimated; see [Memory statistics](#memory-statistics) |

## Bounding by size

Object sizes can't be measured reliably at runtime, so to bound the cache by memory you say what an entry costs:

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<MethodCacheMemoryOptions>(o =>
{
    o.MaxMemoryBytes = 256 * 1024 * 1024;   // bound the cache by size instead of by count
    o.Weigher = (key, value) => value is string s ? s.Length * 2 : 64;
});
```

The weigher must be fast, thread-safe and return a non-negative value. Without one, `MaxMemoryBytes` is ignored.

## Memory statistics

With a `Weigher`, `GetStatsAsync().MemoryUsage` is the total weight of the entries, the same number that is checked
against `MaxMemoryBytes`. Without one, it is a rough estimate, chosen with `MemoryCalculationMode`:

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<MethodCacheMemoryOptions>(o =>
{
    o.MemoryCalculationMode = MemoryUsageCalculationMode.Sampling;   // default Fast
    o.SamplingPercentage = 0.05;                                     // default 0.1 (10% of entries)
});
```

| Mode | How `MemoryUsage` is estimated |
|------|--------------------------------|
| `Fast` (default) | From the entry count and the types and lengths of a sample of the values (strings, arrays, collections) |
| `Sampling` | Serializes a sample of the values to JSON and scales the average size by the entry count |
| `Accurate` | Serializes every value to JSON. Despite the name, this is an estimate too |
| `Disabled` | Always 0 |

None of the modes measures the real memory of object graphs, shared references or the GC heap; use the number to see
trends. The sampling options:

- `SamplingPercentage` (default 0.1) is the share of entries in one sample, at most `SamplingMaxEntries` (default
  1024).
- `SamplingRecalculationInterval` (default 100) is the number of statistics reads before a new sample is taken; 1
  samples on every read. In between, the previous average is scaled by the current entry count.
- `AccurateModeRecalculationInterval` (default 1000) is the number of statistics reads between full calculations in
  `Accurate` mode; reads in between get a `Fast` estimate.

## How strict the bound is

Cache hits never wait for eviction. It runs in batches off the read path, so a new entry is stored at once and counted
against `MaxItems` (or `MaxMemoryBytes`) when the next batch applies it. Under any load:

- The counted size or weight is never more than one entry over the bound.
- When writers get ahead of eviction, they wait for it and help with it, so at most `16 × processor count` (at least
  64) inserts, plus two per writing thread, are stored but not yet counted.

Moments after the writes stop, the cache is back within the bound.

## Null values

`null` results are cached by default, so a method that returns `null` isn't run again on every call. Set
`CacheNullValues = false` when `null` means "not there yet" and the next call should try again, or use
[`CacheWhen`](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md) for one method.

## Cached objects are shared

The cache stores the object your method returned and hands the same instance to every caller. Don't change a cached
object; return immutable types such as records, or copies.

Weighted capacity accounting remains nonnegative even for valid weights near `long.MaxValue`. Before an addition could overflow, the engine evicts existing weight; normal capacity/admission behavior is unchanged below that arithmetic limit.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/native-aot.md -->

# Native AOT

MethodCache works in Native AOT and trimmed applications when your cached methods take arguments the decorator can
write into the key itself (see [Keys](#keys) below). The source generator writes the decorators, their registration
and those keys at build time. CI publishes a test application with Native AOT on every change and checks that
caching (with simple, record, collection and `ICacheKeyProvider` arguments), explicit `AutoRegister(ServiceLifetime)` registration and
`[assembly: CacheInterface]` work.

CI also compiles the complete supported signature corpus with Native AOT. This checks generated signatures and
ref safety across all key forms; reflection-based fallback cases retain the runtime limitations described below.

## In-memory caching

Nothing to do: the in-memory cache stores your objects as they are, without serializing them.

## Distributed caching

Values written to Redis or SQL Server are serialized with System.Text.Json. Under Native AOT it needs a
`JsonSerializerContext` that lists every type your cached methods return:

```cs
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Product))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<Product>))]   // every type a cached method returns
public sealed partial class ShopJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext;
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
builder.Services.AddSingleton<ISerializer>(new JsonCacheSerializer(ShopJsonContext.Default.Options));
```

`ISerializer` and `JsonCacheSerializer` are in `MethodCache.Extensibility`. MethodCache can't generate this context
for you, because one source generator can't see another generator's output.

## Keys

Under Native AOT, give cached methods arguments that the decorator writes into the key itself:

- simple values (strings, numbers, `bool`, `Guid`, dates, enums),
- records, classes and structs whose public properties and fields are simple values, passed as exactly the declared
  type (a sealed type is safest: an instance of a derived class goes through the key generator),
- types that implement `ICacheKeyProvider`,
- arrays, lists and sets of those (records and classes in them must be sealed), and dictionaries whose keys and values
  are simple values.

Collection subclasses with their own public state also use the key generator; implement `ICacheKeyProvider` on
these types when using Native AOT. Plain lists, arrays and sets keep their inline keys.

Other arguments, such as interfaces, `object` or collections of collections, go through the key generator, which
serializes them with reflection-based System.Text.Json. Publishing then reports trim and AOT warnings (IL2026,
IL3050) from `MethodCache.Core`, and the call throws `InvalidOperationException` at runtime. Wrap such an argument in a type that
implements `ICacheKeyProvider`, as `TenantId` does in [Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#types-whose-state-is-private).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/testing.md -->

# Testing

The implementation of a cached interface is a plain class: create it directly in unit tests and no caching is
involved.

## Testing with caching

To test the caching itself, such as invalidation tags, build a service provider the way the application does:

```cs
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddSingleton<Database>();
services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();
services.AddMethodCache();
var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider();

// Resolved through the generated decorator, exactly as in the application
var products = provider.CreateScope().ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IProductService>();
```

`ICacheAdministrator` from the same provider lists the entries and their keys, which helps when a test needs to check
what was cached ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## Turning caching off

Register `NoOpCacheManager` after `AddMethodCache()` and every call reaches your implementation:

```cs
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddSingleton<Database>();
services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();
services.AddMethodCache();
services.AddSingleton<ICacheManager, NoOpCacheManager>();   // after AddMethodCache: every call reaches ProductService
```

For code that uses [manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md), pass a `NoOpCacheManager` directly. `GetOrCreateAsync` is an
extension method, so mocking libraries can't intercept it:

```cs
ICacheManager cache = new NoOpCacheManager();   // never caches: the factory runs on every call
var reader = new OrderReader(cache, repository);
```

`NoOpCacheManager` is in `MethodCache.Extensibility`.

## Time

The cache reads the time from the `TimeProvider` registered in the container, if there is one. Register a fake
`TimeProvider`, for example from `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`, to test expiration without waiting.
This includes the background cleanup of the memory cache and, with `MethodCache.HttpCaching`, response freshness,
eviction and the background revalidation timeout.

The web demo uses a shared SQLite database in the temp folder (`methodcache-webdemo-products.db`), so concurrent price updates from either demo instance are atomic. Decimal prices retain full precision. The earlier temporary JSON file is left untouched; the SQLite catalog starts with the demo seed data.


---

<!-- source: docs/security.md -->

# Security

What each package protects against, what it leaves to you, and the tests that hold it to that.

## Release publishing

`build/ci/publish.sh <tag>` retrieves only the configured BWS publishing secret after packing. The
NuGet API key goes to a .NET SDK 10.0.300+ CLI through `NUGET_API_KEY` and `NUGET_SYMBOL_API_KEY`, without appearing in command-line
arguments or shell traces. The BWS token is removed from the upload process's environment; inherited BWS
and both NuGet publishing credentials are removed from build-step environments. The script refuses a release
whose `MethodCache CI` status is not green. `build/ci/tests/test_publish.py` covers these boundaries and
failure paths. The host, release code and SDK remain trusted: this does not isolate malicious code running
under the same OS user from local credential files.

## MethodCache (keys, tags, invalidation)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| A caller crafts an argument (`"1:orders"`, `"a)"`, a newline) so that their call gets another call's key and its cached result | Keys separate arguments unambiguously: string parts escape `\` and `:`, `null` is `\0`, records are `(a:b)` with escaped members, and hashed keys length-prefix every value and record the runtime type of values in `object`, base-class or interface slots (`1` and `1L` in an `object[]` differ). JSON and MessagePack key-provider parts and nested strings preserve exact UTF-16 code units, including lone surrogates. Recursive key generation from providers or JSON getters cannot overwrite another invocation's key arguments. Arguments whose only state is private, including fields inherited from base classes, are rejected rather than hashed as an empty object. Framework types are written by their value (`BigInteger`, `IPAddress`, `JsonElement` and the others in [Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#framework-types)), not by public properties such as `BigInteger.Sign`, and any other type from .NET, ASP.NET Core or Microsoft.Extensions in a key, such as `StringBuilder`, is build error MCG018. Overloaded methods include the namespaces of their parameter types, so equally named types from different namespaces cannot share a method identity, and a method name that two interfaces of one hierarchy declare adds the parameter types (and the declaring interface for equal signatures) to the key, so `ILookup.Find(int)` and `ICatalog.Find(string)` cannot share an entry through the `ICatalog` decorator. Collection subclasses include their own public state alongside their elements in every key generator. No argument list produces another method's key or another argument list's key. Fluent versions have a separate namespace, with reserved user-key prefixes escaped, so a crafted raw key cannot reach a versioned entry. |
| An argument that is a secret ends up readable | Keys contain argument values in plain text (hashed keys are not encryption) and appear in the admin endpoints and, if you turn them on, in traces. Don't cache methods that take passwords or tokens; pass an id. |
| A tag built from user text invalidates someone else's entries | **Not prevented.** Tags are plain text: `"user:{userId}"` with the id `"1:orders"` is the same tag that `"user:{userId}:orders"` gives user 1, so invalidating one also removes the other. This only ever removes entries (they are loaded again); it never serves one caller's value to another. Use ids that can't contain your separator (`int`, `Guid`) in tag templates. |
| A load races invalidation and a newer write | Invalidated loads cannot publish over newer entries, even when custom weight calculation stalls or re-enters the cache. Existing callers may finish with their pre-invalidation result; later loads and writes retain their own entry. |
| A tag built from user text clears the whole distributed cache | L2 metadata preserves every UTF-16 code unit, including lone surrogates, so reading a tag cannot change its invalidation identity. A tag is only ever its own tag, whatever characters it holds; the internal "clear everything" marker can't be named by a tag. |
| `*` or `?` in user text widens an invalidation | `InvalidateByTagsAsync`, `InvalidateByKeysAsync` and the admin endpoints match exactly. Only `InvalidateByTagPatternAsync` reads wildcards: never build its pattern from user text. Patterns are matched without regular expressions, so a pattern can't cause catastrophic backtracking. |
| `[CacheKey(UseAsRawKey = true)]` | The argument *is* the key, unescaped, so a caller who controls it can read any other entry with that key. Use it only for keys your code builds. |

## Distributed cache (Redis, SQL Server)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| Corrupt, truncated or crafted bytes in the distributed cache | Read as a miss and loaded again: never an exception for the caller, never a `null` that wasn't stored, and lengths in the data are checked against its size before anything is allocated. |
| Stored data names a type to create (deserialization gadgets) | `JsonCacheSerializer` reads the method's declared type and ignores `$type`. `MessagePackCacheSerializer` uses the contractless resolver with `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData` and refuses typeless payloads. Keep it that way if you pass your own options. |
| Someone who can write to Redis or SQL Server | **Not prevented.** They can store any well-formed value, which every instance will serve. Custom method-result providers must implement backend-atomic invalidation stamps through `IAtomicInvalidationStore`; plain read-modify-write providers are rejected. The distributed cache is trusted: protect it like your database (authentication, TLS, network rules), and give each application its own `KeyPrefix`. Redis uses injective escaping before UTF-8 encoding, including for atomic stamps, so different UTF-16 keys cannot alias through replacement characters. SQL Server hashes exact UTF-16 cache keys so collation cannot alias distinct data or invalidation metadata keys, including NULs and trailing spaces. SQL Server also scopes backplane messages and cleanup by that exact prefix, independently of database collation. Automatic initialization rejects missing, nullable or incorrectly typed scope columns; it requires `binary(32) NOT NULL`. |
| Invalidations evicted from the store | A store that evicts a tag or removal stamp under memory pressure makes the entries it invalidated valid again (for example data cached before a permission change). Run Redis with `maxmemory-policy noeviction` or a Redis of its own; see [Keep invalidations from being evicted](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#keep-invalidations-from-being-evicted). |
| Backplane messages | Carry keys and tags in lossless UTF-16 frames, so lone surrogates cannot change invalidation identity and newlines cannot forge another message type. Messages from another MethodCache version are rejected with one warning, without logging their contents. Anyone who can publish on the channel can invalidate entries, so the same trust applies. |

## MethodCache.AspNetCore (admin endpoints)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| An endpoint reachable without authorization | `MapMethodCacheAdmin` requires an authorization policy name, and every endpoint it maps requires that policy: anonymous callers get 401, signed-in users without it 403. A test reads the app's route table and checks every mapped endpoint, so a new endpoint without the policy fails a test. |
| A cross-site form or `fetch` without preflight calls `invalidate` with the admin's cookie | `POST invalidate` only accepts `application/json`, which a browser sends cross-site only after a CORS preflight; forms and `text/plain` get 415. The `DELETE` endpoints need a preflight too. Don't add a CORS policy that allows these routes from other origins. |
| Cached values leak through the admin API | Entries are listed with key, value type, age, time to live, tags and size, never the value. Keys contain argument values (see above), so the policy should admit only operators. |
| Bad input | A missing `key` or an out-of-range `limit` is 400, an empty or blank tag list is 400, and keys and tags are matched literally, never as patterns. |

The health check reports counts only. If you map it with a detailed response writer, put that endpoint behind
authorization too.

## MethodCache.HttpCaching

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| Two users of one `HttpClient` get each other's responses (private cache, the default) | `Authorization` and `Cookie` are part of every response's key, including values that don't parse as a credential, so each caller only gets responses fetched with their own headers. `AddHttpCaching()` disables automatic cookies on known transports; explicitly supplied cookie headers isolate callers. Unknown transports, and handlers inside the primary transport, bypass caching unless explicitly verified and opted in with `AllowUnverifiedTransport`. A directly constructed cache handler also bypasses known transports with automatic cookies enabled. An empty header and no header are different callers too. Header values are individually length-framed, so a comma inside one value cannot alias two separate values. |
| A 200 or 304 changes response privacy or variant selection | Revalidated representations are checked again: `no-store`, `Vary: *` or shared-cache `private` removes previous responses. An omitted `Vary` on a 304 keeps its previous value. Unstorable full replacements also retire the old body, and selection-rule changes retire its URL epoch once so a newer concurrent publication remains reachable, including when old-entry deletion fails after a successful rotation. |
| A shared cache (`IsSharedCache = true`) stores a personal response | Responses marked `private`, and responses to requests with any `Authorization` header, are not stored unless they say `public`, `s-maxage` or `must-revalidate` (RFC 9111 section 3.5). |
| Stale content bypasses required validation | Response or request `no-cache` requires successful validation even with stale-while-revalidate or stale-if-error enabled; origin failures propagate. |
| A cached response hands out a session | `Set-Cookie` is never stored. The caller the origin answered gets it, including on a `304`; nobody answered from the cache does. |
| Responses that vary by a header (tenant, language) get mixed | `Vary` and `KeyHeaders` keep one response per value. `Vary: *` is never served from the cache. |
| A write leaves another caller's stale copy, or serves one caller's copy to another after it | A successful `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` changes the publication generation for every caller. Older in-flight responses write into an obsolete namespace. Shared generation records must be retained and protected from eviction; invalidation failures propagate to the caller. |
| Two URLs share an entry | The key is the method and the full URL, with reserved characters kept escaped (`%2F`, `%3F` and `/`, `?` are different URLs). |
| A followed redirect hands one caller's response to another | The transport drops `Authorization` on a redirect and changes the URL on the same message. A response that ended at another URL or method is never stored under the URL that was requested, and entries are keyed on the request as the caller sent it, before the transport changed it. |
| A malformed `Cache-Control` hides `private` or `no-store` | A `Cache-Control` or `Vary` field the parser rejects, also next to a valid one, makes the response not storable instead of being ignored. |
| Clients that get caching from `ConfigureHttpClientDefaults` share entries | Each client's handler gets its own name, so clients (often one per tenant or API key) never read each other's entries. |
| Crafted entries in the distributed HTTP cache | Read as a miss, with every length checked against the data. As above, whoever can write that cache can store any response. |

Not guaranteed, by design:

- In a **shared** cache, a response stored for an anonymous request is served to authorized requests for the same URL
  too, and responses that depend on cookies are shared unless the origin sends `Vary: Cookie` or `private`. That is
  what RFC 9111 specifies for a shared cache. Add `Cookie` or `Authorization` to `KeyHeaders` when your origin
  personalises without saying so.
- Anonymous callers of a private cache are one caller: they share responses.
- Debug and warning logs include request URLs. Don't put secrets in query strings.

## MethodCache.OpenTelemetry

With the default options, nothing that identifies a person or an argument leaves the process:

| Signal | Recorded by default | Opt-in |
|---|---|---|
| Span attributes | method id, hit or miss, TTL, group, version, number of keys invalidated; on failure the exception type, message and stack trace | `RecordCacheKeys` (a SHA-256 hash of the key, or the key itself with `HashCacheKeys = false`); `RecordCacheTags` (tags and invalidation patterns, which contain argument values when built from templates) |
| Span baggage | the correlation and invalidation ids you set | `ExportSensitiveData` adds the user and tenant ids |
| Metrics | dimensions `method`, `group`, `version`, `error.type`, and `client` and `outcome` for HTTP caching | none: tags, keys and URLs are never metric dimensions |

Cache spans copy the `http.*` and `url.*` attributes of the request span they belong to; turn off
`EnableHttpCorrelation` if those hold data your traces shouldn't. Exception messages come from your own code; keep
personal data out of them. Setting the user or tenant id to `null` or an empty string removes it, so a worker that
handles one message after another doesn't attribute a message without a user to the previous message's user.

## The tests

CI checkout collection and result reuse have a separate boundary from application caching. The collector only
removes coordinator-owned idle macOS clones with verified origin/full commit, terminal job results, and no
source changes or unexpected local data. It refuses redirected roots/results and keeps active checkouts and
unknown directories. Reuse requires the full SHA and all expected valid job exits; partial archives, failed
results and symlinked exit files cannot become a passing status. The regression suite under `build/ci/tests`
tests these protections. Build jobs still execute repository code as the build-server user; the collector is
not a sandbox for malicious pull requests.

Each row above is pinned by a test: `AdminEndpointSecurityTests` (ASP.NET Core), `HttpCacheIsolationTests`,
`HttpCacheEdgeCaseTests` and `UntrustedEntryTests` (HTTP caching), `TelemetryDefaultsLeakTests` and `TelemetryPrivacyTests` (OpenTelemetry), `KeyInjectionPropertyTests` and
`DistributedCacheSecurityTests` (keys, tags and the distributed cache).

MessagePack key identity includes derived state in nested base-class/interface slots and collections. `PolymorphicKeyReviewTests` checks that distinct derived argument data cannot share a cache key.

HTTP age arithmetic saturates during response correction and resident-time accumulation, so an extreme upstream Age value cannot overflow the freshness calculation. `ResponseDelayReviewTests` covers these input boundaries.

Bulk publication guards are tested during key, tag and clear invalidation; in-flight batch results cannot resurrect invalidated entries. Collection-state properties and the generator signature corpus cover tenant/scope state on collection subclasses.

Persistent SQL insert locks, including other scopes sharing the table, cannot hold back newer invalidations or other committed gaps. The non-skipping `LongTransactionReviewTests` and `LockedGapReviewTests` in `MethodCache.Core.Tests/FaultInjection` exercise the production gap-discovery protocol without a database. Linked SQL integration variants additionally inject real locks through repeated polls and verify late commit/rollback recovery.

## Generated contract and registration boundaries

Generated code uses a versioned facade and captures policy, prefix and local publication generation together.
A key builder from another binding/snapshot is rejected before lookup. Retired loads cannot publish or serve
an old-generation fail-safe value. Descriptor/module state is separate from each container's live policy,
keyed binding and background scope. Unknown contracts fail before descriptor/factory execution; ambiguous
modules, candidates and unsupported cacheable bindings fail instead of choosing an implementation implicitly.
The corresponding tests are GeneratedContractTests, QuickStartRegistrationTests and the semantic signature corpus.


---

<!-- source: docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

To see what is actually cached, list the entries with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or `GET /methodcache/entries`,
and the effective policy of every method with `GetMethods()` or `GET /methodcache/methods` ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## The method runs on every call

- **The attribute is on the class.** `[Cache]` is read from the interface only. The analyzer reports
  [MC0001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0001) and its code fix moves the attribute.
- **The service was registered after `AddMethodCache()`.** Call `AddMethodCache()` after your own registrations.
- **An open generic registration.** `AddScoped(typeof(IRepository<>), ...)` is not decorated; register the closed
  types ([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#3-register-it)).
- **The caller doesn't use the interface.** The cache is a decorator around the interface. Resolving or injecting the
  class itself, or calling the method from inside the class (`this.GetAsync(...)`), skips it.
- **The arguments differ between calls.** A `DateTime.Now`, a new `Guid` or a request object with a unique id in it
  makes every key different. List the keys to check ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)).
- **`StringBuilder`, `CultureInfo` or another framework type in an argument** is build error
  [MCG018](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg018): its key would not follow its value. Pass a string or an id instead
  ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#framework-types)).
- **The result is not stored on purpose:** a `CacheWhen` predicate rejected it, the result is `null` with
  `CacheNullValues = false`, or the call threw. Exceptions are never cached.
- **A test registered `NoOpCacheManager`**, which never caches ([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md)).

## Old data after an update

- **The tags don't match.** `[CacheInvalidate]` removes only the tags it lists. Compare them with the cached methods'
  tags.
- **A tag template isn't filled in.** The name in braces must be a parameter of that method:
  [MCG009](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg009) warns about unknown names. A property path such as `"{product.Id}"` is
  not a template and stays literal ([MCG015](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg015)); pass the id as a parameter.
- **The update method threw.** Invalidation runs only after the method completes successfully.
- **The data changed outside the interface**, for example in another service or a database job. Invalidate from that
  code with `ICacheManager.InvalidateByTagsAsync` ([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#from-code)).
- **You run several instances** with only the in-memory cache. Each instance has its own cache; add
  [Redis or SQL Server](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md) so invalidations reach all of them. With a custom
  `IDistributedCache`, also register an `IBackplane`.
- **Fail-safe returned an expired value** because the method failed ([Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md)).

## Results stay out of the distributed cache

A method whose result type is `object`, an interface or an abstract class (`Task<IShape>`, `Task<List<object>>`) has
warning [MCG019](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg019). The serializer can't tell which class to create when it reads
such a result back, so when a distributed cache is used the default round-trip check keeps these results in memory
only, and each instance loads its own. Return a concrete type, such as `Task<Circle>` or `Task<List<Product>>`.

## Keys look different than expected

List the keys with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or `GET /methodcache/entries`, and build the key you expect with
`MethodCacheKeys.For(...)` to compare them. [Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md) explains how each argument becomes part of
a key.

## A change in appsettings.json has no effect

- `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration(builder.Configuration)` must be called.
- The key under `Services` must be the method id: the interface's full name, a dot and the method name. An unknown id
  is logged as a warning at startup. `GET /methodcache/methods` lists the ids.
- A runtime override for the method wins over the file ([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)).
- An invalid value in a reloaded file is logged as an error, and the previous policies stay.

## Exceptions

| Exception | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `InvalidOperationException` when building a key | An argument type has only private state, so every value would get the same key. Implement `ICacheKeyProvider` ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#types-whose-state-is-private)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` at startup | `OnHit`, `OnMiss`, `WithMetrics` or `When` configured for a `[Cache]` method. They apply to `GetOrCreateAsync` only. Without a generic host, the first cached call throws |
| `InvalidOperationException` from `AddMethodCache` naming two assemblies | Two assemblies list the same interface in `[assembly: CacheInterface]`; pass the one whose policies apply ([Caching third-party code](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md)) |
| `NotSupportedException` from `InvalidateByTagPatternAsync` | Pattern invalidation doesn't work with a distributed cache. Invalidate exact tags |
| `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `WithDuration` | Durations must be positive. An override can't turn caching off; invalidate instead |
| `InvalidOperationException` at startup naming a `MethodCache:` path | An invalid value, an unknown setting name, a single value for `Tags`, `Metadata` or a section that holds settings, nested settings under a single setting, or a time span without `:` in the `MethodCache` section |

## A caller changed a cached object, and others see the change

The cache hands the same instance to every caller. Return immutable types such as records, or copies
([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#cached-objects-are-shared)).

## Build errors and warnings

Every `MC` and `MCG` diagnostic, with what to do about it, is in [Build diagnostics](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md -->

# Build diagnostics

MethodCache checks your attributes when you build. Errors mean the method would not be cached as written, so the
build stops; warnings point at attributes that do nothing. Every diagnostic links to its section below, and the ones
marked **Code fix** can be fixed from the light bulb in Visual Studio, Rider or VS Code.

| Id | Severity | Summary | Code fix |
|----|----------|---------|----------|
| [MC0001](#mc0001) | Warning | `[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` on a class member | Move to the interface |
| [MC0004](#mc0004) | Error | A time span that is not a positive `TimeSpan` | |
| [MCG001](#mcg001) | Error | `[Cache]` on a `void` method | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG002](#mcg002) | Error | `[Cache]` on `Task`/`ValueTask` without a result | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG003](#mcg003) | Error | `[Cache]` with reference parameters or returns | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG004](#mcg004) | Error | `[Cache]` and `[CacheInvalidate]` on the same method | |
| [MCG005](#mcg005) | Warning | `[CacheInvalidate]` without tags | |
| [MCG006](#mcg006) | Error | `[Cache]` with pointer or function pointer parameters or returns, including arrays of them | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG007](#mcg007) | Error | `[Cache]` with ref struct or potentially ref-like parameters or returns | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG009](#mcg009) | Warning | A tag names a parameter the method does not have | Use the closest parameter |
| [MCG010](#mcg010) | Error | `[assembly: CacheInterface]` names a type it can't decorate | |
| [MCG011](#mcg011) | Error | `[assembly: CacheInterface]` lists a method it can't cache | |
| [MCG012](#mcg012) | Error | The same interface in more than one `[assembly: CacheInterface]` | |
| [MCG013](#mcg013) | Error | An interface with static or non-public abstract members | |
| [MCG014](#mcg014) | Error | `[Cache]` on a lazy sequence | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG015](#mcg015) | Warning | A tag placeholder that is not a parameter name, such as `{product.Id}` | |
| [MCG016](#mcg016) | Warning | A tag placeholder matches several parameter names without an exact spelling match | |
| [MCG017](#mcg017) | Warning | `[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` on a `static`, non-public or `sealed` interface member | |
| [MCG018](#mcg018) | Error | A key argument, element or member has a framework type without a key form, such as `StringBuilder` | |
| [MCG019](#mcg019) | Warning | A cached result type of `object`, an interface or an abstract class, which a distributed cache can't restore | |

## MC0001

`[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` is on a class, struct or record member. MethodCache generates a decorator for the
interface, so it only reads attributes on interface methods, and this one is ignored.

```csharp
public interface IUserService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00")]      // here
    Task<User> GetAsync(int id);
}

public class UserService : IUserService
{
    public Task<User> GetAsync(int id) => ...;   // not here
}
```

**Code fix:** moves the attribute to the interface method the member implements (adding the `using` if needed), or
removes it when the member implements no interface. To cache an interface you don't own, see the
[third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MC0004

`Duration`, `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`, `FailSafe` or `FailSafeTimeout` on `[Cache]` or
`[assembly: CacheInterface]` is not a positive time span. Use the `TimeSpan` format: `"00:05:00"` (five minutes),
`"01:00:00"` (an hour) or `"1.00:00:00"` (a day). `FailSafe` also accepts `"off"`.

## MCG001

`[Cache]` on a `void` method: there is no result to cache. Return the value, or remove `[Cache]`. If the method
changes data, you probably want `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` instead.

## MCG002

`[Cache]` on a method returning `Task` or `ValueTask` without a result. Return `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`, or remove
`[Cache]`. A write method usually wants `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` instead.

## MCG003

`[Cache]` on a method with `ref`, `out` or `in` parameters, or a `ref` / `ref readonly` return.
A cached value cannot preserve references or set an `out` value. Pass and return values by value, for example as a record.

## MCG004

`[Cache]` and `[CacheInvalidate]` on the same method. A method either reads (cached) or writes (invalidates); keep
the one that matches what it does.

## MCG005

`[CacheInvalidate]` without tags removes nothing. List the tags of the cached methods it should clear:

```csharp
[Cache(Tags = new[] { "users", "user:{id}" })]
Task<User> GetAsync(int id);

[CacheInvalidate(Tags = new[] { "users", "user:{id}" })]
Task UpdateAsync(int id, User user);
```

## MCG006

`[Cache]` on a method with pointer or function pointer parameters or returns, including arrays of them such as
`int*[]`. These cannot be stored as cached values or keys; use a value or an array of values. Unsupported methods, and
any other member of the interface that uses a pointer, are still forwarded through an unsafe implementation.

## MCG007

`[Cache]` on a method with `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>` or other ref struct parameters or returns. These cannot be
stored in a cache; use an array, `Memory<T>` or a string. This also applies to a type parameter with `allows ref struct` when that parameter is used as an argument or return value.

## MCG009

A tag such as `"user:{userId}"` names a parameter the method does not have, so the braces stay literal text and every
call shares that tag. The name between the braces must match a parameter name: the exact spelling first, otherwise a
single case-insensitive match. A name that matches several parameters only by case is [MCG016](#mcg016).

A template takes a parameter name only; a property path such as `"{product.Id}"` is reported as [MCG015](#mcg015).

**Code fix:** offers the closest parameter names, so `"user:{usrId}"` becomes `"user:{userId}"`.

## MCG010

`[assembly: CacheInterface]` names a type MethodCache can't decorate: a class, a generic interface, an interface that
is not accessible, one with static abstract or non-public abstract members, or one declared in your own project (put `[Cache]` on its methods
instead). It is also reported when the attribute lists no methods. See the [third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MCG011

`[assembly: CacheInterface]` lists a method that is missing, overloaded or static, or one that `[Cache]` would reject:
it returns nothing to cache, has `ref`, `out`, `in`, pointer or ref struct parameters, a framework type without a key
form ([MCG018](#mcg018)), or returns a lazy sequence. Use
`nameof(IClient.Method)` so a rename is caught by the compiler. See the
[third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MCG012

The same interface is listed in more than one `[assembly: CacheInterface]`. List each interface once, with all its
methods in the same attribute.

## MCG013

The interface has static abstract members, or non-public abstract members that cannot be forwarded to the decorated
instance. Move the cached methods to an interface without them. Non-public default methods are supported because they
remain on the interface, and so are nested helper types declared inside the interface.

## MCG014

`[Cache]` on a method returning `IEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`. The cached value would be
the lazy sequence itself, which runs the query again on every enumeration. Return a materialized collection, such as
`Task<List<T>>`, `Task<IReadOnlyList<T>>` or `T[]`, and call `ToListAsync()` (or similar) in the implementation.

## MCG015

A tag has braces that look like a template but don't hold a plain parameter name: a property path such as
`"product:{product.Id}"`, spaces such as `"{ id }"`, or a format such as `"{day:yyyy-MM-dd}"`. Templates take a
parameter name only, so the braces stay literal text and every call shares the same tag. Write `"product:{id}"` and
add the value as its own parameter, as `UpdateAsync(int id, Product product)` does in
[Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md). For `[assembly: CacheInterface]` both MCG009 and MCG015 are reported on the
attribute.

## MCG016

The placeholder has no exact parameter match and more than one case-insensitive match, such as `{NAME}` for
parameters `name` and `Name`. Use the intended parameter's exact spelling. Until corrected, the placeholder remains
literal in both cached tags and invalidation.

## MCG017

`[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` is on an interface member the decorator can't intercept: a `static` member, a
`private` or other non-public member with a body, or a `sealed` one. The decorator implements the interface for a
class, and a class can't implement those members, so calls to them never reach the cache and the attribute does
nothing. Put the attribute on a public interface method without `static`, `private` or `sealed` (one without a body,
or a public default method), or remove it.

## MCG018

A key argument has a type from .NET itself, ASP.NET Core or Microsoft.Extensions (an assembly named `System.*`,
`Microsoft.AspNetCore.*` or `Microsoft.Extensions.*`) that the cache key can't be written from: the
argument itself, an element of a collection or tuple, or a public property or field of your own type, such as
`StringBuilder`, `CultureInfo`, `Stream`, `Type` or a `Func<T>`. Their public properties don't hold their value, or the
value can change after the call (a `StringBuilder`), so two different arguments could share a key and one caller
would get another's result. The message names the value, such as `'note.Text' is a 'StringBuilder'`.

Pass a value that identifies it instead, such as a string, an id or a culture name, or wrap it in a type that
implements `ICacheKeyProvider` (see [Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#framework-types)). The key ignores the rest of the
arguments when one has `[CacheKey(UseAsRawKey = true)]`, so the error is not reported then.

Framework types with a key form are written by their value: `Guid`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeSpan`,
`DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`, `Half`, `Int128`, `UInt128`, `BigInteger`, `Complex`, `Uri`, `Version`, `IPAddress` and
`JsonElement` (as its JSON, so whitespace doesn't count), `Index`, `Range`, `Vector2`, `Vector3`, `Vector4`,
`Quaternion`, `Plane`, `Matrix3x2`, `Matrix4x4`, and ASP.NET Core's `PathString`, `QueryString` and `HostString`, as
well as arrays, collections, `Memory<T>`, tuples and `KeyValuePair` of those. Models from other libraries, such as
an SDK's classes in a `Microsoft.*` namespace, are not framework types: they are written by their public properties
like your own.

## MCG019

The cached method's result type, after `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`, is `object`, an interface such as `IComparable` or
`IShape`, or an abstract class, or has one as an element (`List<object>`). A distributed cache stores results as
JSON or MessagePack of the declared type, which can't say which class to create when it reads them back. When a
distributed cache is used, the default round-trip check finds that such a result doesn't read back, and keeps it in the
in-memory cache only. Collection interfaces such as
`IReadOnlyList<Product>` are fine; they are read back as a list.

Return a concrete type, such as `Task<Product>` or `Task<List<Product>>`, to share the results through the distributed
cache. When only the in-memory cache is used, or memory-only is what you want, suppress the warning with
`#pragma warning disable MCG019` or `<NoWarn>` in the project.


---

<!-- source: docs/migration-from-imemorycache.md -->

# Migrating from IMemoryCache

With `IMemoryCache`, every cached method holds the same pattern: build a key, try the cache, load, store, and remember
every key to remove when data changes. MethodCache moves that into an attribute on the interface.

<table>
<tr><th>Before: IMemoryCache</th><th>After: MethodCache</th></tr>
<tr><td>

```cs
public async Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id)
{
    var key = $"user:{id}";
    if (_cache.TryGetValue(key, out User? user))
        return user!;

    // Two callers can both miss and both hit the database
    user = await _db.LoadUserAsync(id);
    _cache.Set(key, user, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10));
    return user;
}

public async Task RenameAsync(int id, string name)
{
    await _db.RenameAsync(id, name);
    _cache.Remove($"user:{id}");
    // ...and every other key that held this user
}
```

</td><td>

```cs
[Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["user:{id}"])]
Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id);

[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["user:{id}"])]
Task RenameAsync(int id, string name);
```

</td></tr>
</table>

## Steps

1. Add the `MethodCache` package and call `builder.Services.AddMethodCache()` after your registrations
   ([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)).
2. If the class has no interface, extract one. Callers must use the interface, because the cache is a decorator around
   it.
3. Move the caching settings to `[Cache]` on the interface method, and delete the cache code from the implementation.
4. Replace each `Remove(key)` with `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` on the method that changes the data, and give the
   cached methods matching tags ([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md)).
5. Code that can't move to an attribute, such as a cached call in the middle of a method, uses
   `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync` with the key it already has ([Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md)).

Migrate one service at a time; both caches can run side by side.

## What maps to what

| IMemoryCache | MethodCache |
|--------------|-------------|
| `TryGetValue` + `Set` | `[Cache]`, or `GetOrCreateAsync` with your key |
| `SetAbsoluteExpiration` | `Duration` |
| `SetSlidingExpiration` | `SlidingExpiration`, capped by `Duration` |
| `Remove(key)` | `[CacheInvalidate]` with tags, or `InvalidateByKeysAsync` |
| `Size` and `SizeLimit` | `Weigher` and `MaxMemoryBytes` ([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md)) |
| `Priority` | Not needed: W-TinyLFU keeps the entries that are read often |
| `GetOrCreateAsync`, which may run the factory several times at once | Concurrent misses share one call |
| A separate `IDistributedCache` | `AddMethodCacheRedis(...)`, with the memory cache kept in sync ([Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md)) |

## Differences to know

- **Keys are generated** from the method and its arguments ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)). Check that every argument
  that changes the result is a parameter, not a field of the class.
- **`null` is cached** by default. Set `MethodCacheMemoryOptions.CacheNullValues = false` ([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#null-values)) if your old code skipped `null`.
- **Exceptions are never cached**, as before.


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.Redis/README.md -->

# MethodCache.Redis

Install this package and `MethodCache` at the exact same version. Integration packages use Core internals;
do not override their exact Core dependency. Our package smoke tests promote NU1608 to a restore error.

Redis as MethodCache's distributed cache. Results are shared between application instances, and invalidations reach every instance's in-memory cache over Redis pub/sub.

Backplane publication honors its cancellation token before sending and while waiting for a connection or Redis acknowledgement. Cancellation after a publish was sent cannot recall that message.

## Usage

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
```

With options:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis(options =>
{
    options.Configuration = "redis1:6379,redis2:6379,password=...";
    options.KeyPrefix = "orders-api:";   // the backplane channel follows: orders-api:invalidations
});
```

MethodCache keeps its own cache and connection, so your app's `IDistributedCache` and Redis settings are left alone. The connection opens on first use, so the application starts while Redis is down. It uses `BacklogPolicy.FailFast`, so a cache miss runs your method instead of waiting for Redis. When a connection factory of yours throws (Redis was down at first use, say), the next call asks it again, and the backplane keeps trying to connect and subscribe (after 1 second, then twice as long each time, up to 30 seconds), logging a warning for each failure, until it succeeds or the application stops. Once subscribed after a failure, it clears this instance's in-memory cache, as after a reconnect, since invalidations other instances sent meanwhile never arrived.

To share a connection your app already has instead:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis(options =>
    options.ConnectionMultiplexerFactory = sp => sp.GetRequiredService<IConnectionMultiplexer>());
```

MethodCache doesn't dispose a shared connection; disposing the service provider only removes MethodCache's own
subscriptions (`DisposeAsync` waits for that). A cancelled Redis unsubscribe acknowledgement does not fail application shutdown; the handler has already been removed locally.

## How it works

- Entries are stored through `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis`, so values are written without extra copies.
- MethodCache reads Redis on an in-memory miss and writes new results to both.
- Invalidating a key removes it from Redis. Invalidating a tag stores the time of the invalidation, and entries with that tag written before it are treated as missing, so no tag sets are kept in Redis.
- Invalidation times are written with one Lua script, so an older invalidation that arrives late never undoes a newer one.
- Every invalidation is also published on the backplane channel, so every instance drops its in-memory copies at once.
- Pub/sub delivers nothing while a connection is down. When the connection comes back, the instance clears its in-memory cache and reads entries from Redis again.
- Keys with unpaired UTF-16 surrogates or backslashes are escaped, so two different keys never share a Redis key. Other keys are stored unchanged.

## Memory and eviction

Invalidations are stored as expiring keys beside the entries. If Redis evicts one under memory pressure, the entries it
invalidated are served again by every instance until they expire. Set `maxmemory-policy noeviction` on the Redis
MethodCache uses (or give it a Redis of its own) and enough memory: every MethodCache key has a time to live, so
`volatile-lru` and the other `volatile-*` policies, the default of some managed Redis services, can evict them too. A
full Redis with `noeviction` refuses writes, which MethodCache handles like an outage. See
[Keep invalidations from being evicted](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#keep-invalidations-from-being-evicted).

## When Redis is down

MethodCache keeps answering from memory and your methods; Redis never fails or stalls a call. Each call is capped at
`OperationTimeout` (1 second), Redis is skipped for `CircuitBreakerDuration` (10 seconds) after a failure, and
invalidations are queued and retried instead of throwing. The first failure and the recovery are logged.

The [distributed cache guide](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md)
covers outages, consistency between instances, MessagePack serialization, limits and the `DistributedCacheOptions`
that tune all of this.

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `Configuration` | `localhost:6379` | StackExchange.Redis configuration string |
| `ConnectionMultiplexerFactory` | none | Returns an existing connection to share instead of opening one |
| `KeyPrefix` | `methodcache:` | Prefix for every key MethodCache writes |
| `EnableBackplane` | `true` | Send invalidations to other instances over pub/sub |
| `BackplaneChannel` | `KeyPrefix` + `invalidations` | Pub/sub channel; applications with different key prefixes get different channels |


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.SqlServer/README.md -->

# MethodCache.SqlServer

Install this package and `MethodCache` at the exact same version. Integration packages use Core internals;
do not override their exact Core dependency. Our package smoke tests promote NU1608 to a restore error.

SQL Server as MethodCache's distributed cache. Results are shared between application instances, and invalidations reach every instance's in-memory cache through a table that each instance polls.

## Why this package

- **One shared cache for every instance.** Results live in each instance's memory and in SQL Server, so a result one instance computed is a hit for the others, and survives restarts.
